turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on back. I'll grab vitals before Dr. Shah sees you. Left arm alright for the cuff?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Left is fine. I've been sitting out there kind of panicking, so don't be shocked if it's high.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-six, pulse is seventy-eight, oxygen is ninety-eight percent. Reasonable, given the nerves.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is eighty-six bad? I usually think of myself as lower. What medicines do you have listed for me?
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sumatriptan fifty milligrams as needed. No daily medicines on the list.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty isn't right. That was years ago. The tablets I take are a hundred milligrams. The chart never got changed.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll flag fifty in the record versus a hundred from you. Are you taking anything else?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Tylenol, paracetamol, extra strength. Two tablets, so five hundred... no, each is five hundred, so a thousand milligrams. Most days.
[SEG0009] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Acetaminophen a thousand milligrams, got it. She'll be right with you.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. Sounds like these headaches have really been on your mind. What's been going on?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Migraines since I was twenty-five... ugh, no, I always get that wrong. They started when I was thirty. I'm forty-six, so sixteen years. This stretch is different and it's freaking me out.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Different in what way, when you first open your eyes?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It's already there. Both sides, not just the left. Worse in the morning, and I've vomited with it before I even eat.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): The vomiting only happens with those morning headaches?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Three mornings in the last couple of weeks, and I feel wrung out after while the pain just sits there. Is that a brain tumor? I googled, which I know is stupid.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not a stupid fear. From what you're describing it isn't the first thing I think of, but I want the whole picture before I say more. How many mornings a week?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Five out of seven. The vomiting isn't every one of those.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Before this change, how often were the old migraines?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a month, maybe, those old one-sided ones. This newer morning headache, I almost said a month, but no, six weeks, and it's about five days a week since my sister's wedding.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, six weeks. Any weakness, trouble speaking, or double vision?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No weakness, I can talk fine, no double vision. I've been checking.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever, stiff neck, or a headache that peaked in a second?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, neck's fine, and it builds, it doesn't thunderclap.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you taking when it hits?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan, the hundred milligram tablets, four or five days a week. And Tylenol a thousand milligrams by mouth, two or three times a day, nearly every day. That's too much, right? Am I causing this?
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): You might be feeding it, yes. Our chart still says sumatriptan fifty milligrams. Is the bottle in your bag?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it's at home. My husband looked at the label, it says one hundred. So which is it, fifty or a hundred? Could the wrong number be dangerous?
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't pick one without the bottle. Don't double the dose while it's unclear. Does the sumatriptan still help?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): The old ones, yes. These morning headaches, barely. Tylenol takes the edge off for about an hour. Should I have gone to the ER instead?
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't think the ER is where you need to be today. Any other medicines, a blood pressure pill, contraception?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else. Two cups of coffee in the morning. No new supplements.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no allergies.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Morning pain makes me ask about sleep. Does your husband say you snore, or that you seem tired all day?

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Both, and he won't drop it, chainsaw snoring and he says I'm exhausted. I don't buy the exhausted part. I'm a bookkeeper, full days, and I'm not sleepy at the desk. Can we not get lost in the snoring?
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We won't. Are you having any daytime sleepiness at all?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm not tired in the daytime. The snoring I'll admit, he played me a recording, I snore. That's embarrassing, not why I'm here.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any gasping at night, or weight going up?

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't gasp, and my weight is stable. Last week my left eye felt weird for a day, then it went back to normal. Was that a mini stroke? It scared me, then it just vanished.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): A weird eye feeling that cleared in a day isn't a mini stroke on its own. I'm going to examine you, and then I'll answer the scan questions directly.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Please. MRI or CT, how soon, is the radiation bad, I wrote it all down and then lost the paper.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Follow my finger for me. Pupils are equal and reactive to light. Face moves evenly, and your tongue stays midline.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Are the pupils the part that would show pressure? Sorry, keep going.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): They help with that, yes. Your eyes track together and I'm not seeing double vision. Squeeze my fingers, push your feet down. Strength is full in both arms and both legs, reflexes are symmetric.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Full means normal, right? I need the plain word.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, strength and reflexes are normal. Finger to your nose, that's smooth. Walk down and back... gait is steady. Neck is not stiff.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. So what do you actually think is going on?

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Working impression, this is your migraine pattern changing, and medication overuse is likely part of it with near-daily Tylenol plus sumatriptan most days. I can't completely exclude something structural because of the morning vomiting, but a mass is less likely with this exam.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Less likely still isn't zero. Are you ordering the MRI now? What if waiting makes it worse?

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not ordering imaging today. If the morning vomiting is still happening over the next two weeks, or you get weakness, vision loss, or a sudden severe headache, then we do a brain MRI. I'd rather not start with a CT, more radiation and it answers this less well.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): If I vomit again tomorrow, is that the two weeks or do I go to the ER in the morning?

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tomorrow morning alone doesn't send you to the ER. If vomiting keeps showing up through these two weeks, call us and we'll set up the MRI. If the headache turns sudden and extreme, or there's weakness or you can't see right, that's the emergency room the same day.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): What about the pills? If I stop sumatriptan I'll be in agony. Do I taper? Is there something safer you can prescribe today?

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): No new prescription today, and don't stop cold. Limit acetaminophen and sumatriptan each to no more than two days a week. If you still can't live with that, a preventive is a conversation for the next visit, not this one.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. So the other days I just lie in the dark? And I should bring the bottle, yes? My husband will also ask about a sleep study.

[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bring the sumatriptan bottle so we can settle the dose. Dark room, fluids, rest, and don't add extra Tylenol on the off days. I'm not ordering a sleep study. You aren't sleepy in the daytime, so that isn't the move.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): When am I supposed to come back? If I feel better can I skip it? I don't want to waste your time, but I also don't want to miss something.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks either way, whether the mornings settle or not. We'll review the pattern and the bottle. If the MRI ends up booked, we'll time that visit with the result.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Two weeks. I'll try not to google tonight. Thank you for not making me feel ridiculous.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
